title: World War One
examples: What were the main reasons countries fought in World War One?
Can you explain what life was like in the trenches?
How did the war actually end in 1918?

explain.say: The war had several big causes. Militarism meant building up armies and weapons.
Alliances meant countries promised to help each other in a fight. For example, the Triple Entente formed a group.
Imperialism was the competition for colonies and resources around the world. Britain and France wanted many territories.
Nationalism was intense pride in one's nation, sometimes leading to wanting independence. Serbia wanted to unite its people.
Life in the trenches was terrible. Soldiers lived in muddy ditches for years. They faced constant danger and disease.
The war lasted from 1914 to 1918. Battles were often fought in these static trench lines. The fighting was brutal.

faq.q: What were the main causes of World War One?
faq.a: The main causes were a mix of militarism, alliances, imperialism, and intense nationalism among the European powers.
asks: Why did the big European powers fight?

faq.a: The trenches were muddy ditches dug into the ground where soldiers lived and fought for years. They were very dangerous places.
asks: Describe the life in the trenches.

faq.q: How did the war end in 1918?
faq.a: The war ended with an armistice signed in 1918, leading to the defeat of the Central Powers.
asks: What caused the end of the war?

faq.q: Did all the countries involved in the war fight the same way?
faq.a: No, the fighting changed over the years. Early battles were mobile, but they settled into the static trench warfare.
asks: Were the battles always in the trenches?

faq.q: Was the war fought only on land?
faq.a: No, naval battles were also very important parts of the war. Submarines played a major role in the fighting.
asks: Did ships fight in the war?

facts: The war involved major powers like the British Empire, the German Empire, and the Austro-Hungarian Empire.
The assassination of an archduke was the immediate spark for the war in 1914.
Trench warfare involved digging defensive positions along front lines.
The war concluded with an armistice, which marked a ceasefire.

quiz.say: The desire of a country to have many colonies is called:
quiz.why: Imperialism is the competition for colonies and resources around the world.

wrong.0: Nationalism is about pride in one's own people, not owning land.
wrong.1: Militarism is about building up armies and weapons.

quiz.say: What type of fighting characterized the Western Front for years?
quiz.why: The static nature of the fighting meant soldiers lived in ditches called trenches.

wrong.0: Guerrilla tactics involve small, irregular fighting groups.
wrong.2: Mobile warfare involves armies moving quickly across the battlefield.
wrong.3: Naval combat happens on the seas between ships.

quiz.say: The end of the fighting in World War One was marked by:
quiz.why: An armistice is a formal agreement to stop fighting, leading to a ceasefire.

wrong.1: A treaty is a formal, signed peace agreement after the fighting stops.
wrong.2: Surrender is the act of giving up resistance.
wrong.3: A peace treaty is the final document, not the stopping of fighting itself.
